rationale: Evidence from the development race: all 60 trials on oval, s-bend and slalom ended off_track with zero completions. Progress reached only 0.04 to 0.115, and each run recorded one line-loss event. Max error was about 0.061 m, right at the off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m. The robot is leaving the tape quickly, not drifting slowly. Likely causes: (1) base_speed 1.8 is too fast for the steering authority, so the robot slides wide on curves; (2) kp 2.5 with kd 0.1 gives too little correction and too little damping; (3) the sensor array spans only ±0.04 m, so on a moderate offset the outer sensors can drop off the tape and trigger a line loss. Changes: base_speed 1.8 to 1.4 to reduce slide-out on bends; kp 2.5 to 4.0 for a stronger correction per unit of offset; kd 0.1 to 0.5 to damp the faster response; ki stays 0 to avoid windup. Geometry: sensor x spread widened to ±0.06 m (-0.06, -0.03, 0, 0.03, 0.06) so the tape stays under a sensor at larger offsets; sensor_size raised to 0.016 so each sensor sees more tape and the sum stays above the 0.05 line-loss threshold. Wheel_track widened to 0.14 m for more yaw stability, mass lowered to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia and speed up turn response. Expected result: fewer off-track exits, more progress on all three tracks, and possibly the first completions. Trade-off: slower base speed may make it hard to finish under 3 s, so if the robot survives but does not finish, base_speed should rise again. Hypotheses to check: (H1) if steering_oscillation rises sharply, kp is too high relative to kd; (H2) if line_loss_events stay at 1 or more, the sensor spread or size is still too narrow; (H3) if max_error is still near 0.06 on curves, the robot is too fast for its grip and base_speed should drop further. Measurements to see next: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track.
